newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil real ends off 0.1 pct under new mini-band.
newsitem.headline: Brazil real ends off 0.1 pct under new mini-band.

text.p: Brazil's real fell 0.1 percent to close at 1.0501 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market under the new mini-band between 1.0500 and 1.0550 reais per greenback announced on Tuesday by the Central Bank.
Late on Tuesday, the Central Bank announced the new large forex band of between 1.05 and 1.14 reais per dollar, compared with the previous 0.97-1.06 reais per dollar set in January 1996.
After the announcement of the new large band, the Central Bank also announced the new mini-band.
Dealers said the forex market reacted calmly to the new large and mini bands and trade was very quiet today.
"The Central Bank is learning to do transactions without creating nervousness in the market," one dealer said.
Before the session opened today, the Central Bank set a buy/sell auction in which the bank confirmed the new mini-band, eliminating any doubts about the trade level for the reais, dealers said.
Dealers also noted the changes in the band's value finished the speculation started last week over possible changes in forex rate policy.
"The Central Bank announcements yesterday (of the new bands) stopped all the speculation in the market," one trader said.
Late on Wednesday, the Central Bank bought dollars at 1.0500 reais per greenback to drain excess dollars from the market.
Preliminary figures for commercial and financial foreign exchange contracts showed a Wednesday surplus of $295 million.

In the interbank floating rate market, the real dropped 0.08 percent to close at 1.0557 to the dollar, following the lowering in the mini-band. In the illegal parallel market, the real closed at 1.085 per greenback, down 0.28 percent.
